experiment.passage: Upon transfection of the constructs into Hep3B cultured human hepatocellular carcinoma cells, we found that in both orientations, the minor haplotype produced significantly greater luciferase expression than the major haplotype, consistent with the human liver eQTL analyses (Fig. 2b; compare to Fig. 1c). After localizing the haplotype-specific effect to the proximal 2.1 kb of the region (Supplementary Fig. 4), we tested an array of constructs in which single polymorphisms in the minor haplotype were switched to major alleles. We identified the SNP rs12740374 as being sufficient to confer the haplotype-specific effect (Fig. 2c, 3c).

system.tissue_or_cell: Hep3B cultured human hepatocellular carcinoma cells
system.genotype_or_allele: not applicable; reporter constructs contained alternative haplotypes and single-polymorphism changes

experiment.intervention: Transfection of luciferase constructs containing major and minor haplotypes, including constructs in which single minor-haplotype polymorphisms were switched to major alleles
experiment.comparator: Minor versus major haplotype reporter constructs and single-polymorphism alterations
experiment.result: The minor haplotype produced significantly greater luciferase expression; changing rs12740374 was sufficient to confer the haplotype-specific effect. Figure 3 identifies the rs12740374 minor allele as T and the major allele as G.
experiment.scope_supports: A variant-specific allele-comparing result for reporter constructs in Hep3B cells: the T/minor allele was sufficient to confer greater reporter expression than the G/major allele in the tested construct context.
experiment.scope_does_not_test: Does not establish endogenous-locus activity, a specific target gene, or trait mediation.

experiment.passage: Both C228T and C250T generated an identical 11-bp nucleotide stretch (5′-CCCCTTCCGGG-3′) containing a consensus binding site for E-twenty-six (ETS) transcription factors (GGAA, reverse complement) within the TERT promoter region. Because ETS transcription factors may become activated through dysregulation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAP kinase) signaling, we hypothesized that these promoter mutations might augment gene expression. To test this hypothesis, we used a reporter assay system in which the relevant portion of the mutant or wild-type TERT core promoter was cloned upstream of the firefly luciferase gene (2). Here, we tested both a core promoter fragment (−132 to +5 relative to the TSS) and the full core promoter (−200 to +73). In comparison to the wild-type TERT promoter, both mutations conferred approximately two- to fourfold increased transcriptional activity in five distinct cell line contexts (Fig. 1C and fig. S1D). Thus, each mutation was capable of augmenting transcriptional activity from the TERT promoter.

system.tissue_or_cell: A375, RPMI-7951, UACC-62, T24 and HepG2 cell lines
system.genotype_or_allele: Reporter constructs carried wild-type or C228T promoter; cell-line genotypes at the variant are not stated.

experiment.intervention: Compared TERT core promoter reporter constructs carrying C228T with wild-type promoter constructs; promoter fragments were cloned upstream of firefly luciferase.
experiment.result: C228T promoter reporter constructs showed approximately 2–4-fold increased transcriptional activity compared with wild-type constructs across five cell-line contexts.
experiment.scope_supports: C228T increases transcriptional activity in the tested TERT promoter reporter assays.
experiment.scope_does_not_test: Does not establish endogenous TERT regulation, disease mediation, or allele-dependent TF binding.
about_tfs: ETS transcription factors (motif discussed; no binding assay reported in this passage)
